clue.text: Expert Latin speaker leading Northern Italy tour guides

parts.note: Cicero, the Roman orator, was the most celebrated speaker of Latin
N is the standard abbreviation for northern
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A fluent Latinist heads up a party of guides showing visitors around northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Guides were nicknamed after Cicero for their endless eloquent talk; the plural keeps the Italian -I ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicerone is an old word for a guide who shows sightseers around, and its Italian plural ends in I.

clue.text: When aboard taxi, half of English county's a more exotic place

indicators.note: being aboard a vehicle means sitting inside it, so one word goes into another

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: only half of the county's name is used, the first five of its ten letters

parts.note: Lancashire, a county in north-west England, cut to its first half

explanation.surface: Taking a cab through half of Lancashire is claimed to be more exotic than it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England. The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan port city, famous from the Bogart film, is certainly a more exotic destination than Lancashire.

clue.text: Hide cooked meals inside item of furniture

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order
inside tells us the reworked letters go within another word

parts.note: a chair is a piece of furniture
the letters of meals rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to stash a cooked dinner inside a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb telling you to conceal the meals; it is the noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Camel's hair is the animal's coat used as cloth, so loosely a hide or pelt of the camel.

clue.text: Thin and hungry, disposing of starter

indicators.note: getting rid of the starter means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: greedy can mean hungry for food

explanation.surface: Someone skinny and starving who has skipped the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice or figure is thin and slight, like the stem of a reed.

clue.text: Weakening nerves in the sauna, half-bare possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of many arrangements, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of the following word is kept, here its second two letters

parts.note: the back half of this four-letter word

explanation.surface: Sitting half-naked in a sauna might calm your frayed nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of IN THE SAUNA plus the RE from the back of bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurasthenia is an old medical term for nervous exhaustion, a debility of the nervous system.

clue.text: Small boat in rough

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A little vessel caught out on stormy waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' suggests a heavy sea; here it is the noun, a preliminary drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's rough is a quick preliminary drawing, just what a sketch is.

clue.text: Reminders to look up benefits

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look
for the sakes of means for the benefits of

explanation.surface: Mementoes that encourage you to search for advantages.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepsakes are small objects kept as mementoes, things that remind you of a person or event.

clue.text: Seabird circling rocks at sea, finding tropical plant

indicators.note: circling means going all around, so the bird surrounds the other word

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a reef is a ridge of rocks in the sea

explanation.surface: A seabird circling an offshore reef spots a plant growing there.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree ferns are tall ferns with trunk-like stems, typical of tropical and subtropical forests.

clue.text: Localised pain and ache from this rash?

indicators.note: from this tells us the pain is made out of the answer by trading one part for a word of the same meaning

parts.note: a pain confined to one part of the body, above the neck
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A doctor wondering whether a skin rash is to blame for a sore head.
explanation.walkthrough: Work backwards: in the answer, swap LONG for its synonym ACHE and you get HEADACHE, the localised pain. 'rash' looks medical but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing in headlong means acting hastily without thought, which is what rash describes.

clue.text: Reviewed amount raised to secure medicine

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so it is enclosed by the other words

parts.note: a sum is an amount
raised up
MED is short for medicine

explanation.surface: A sum of money was increased to pay for drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum up is to give a brief review of what has been said, as a judge does at a trial.

clue.text: European city to repay, backing shifting a European position?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read right to left
the letter standing for European is moved to a different place in the word

parts.note: to avenge a wrong is to repay it

explanation.surface: A city where a European might relocate, perhaps to pay back a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed, the verb gives EGNEVA; move its leading E (European) one place along to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is the Swiss city on Lake Geneva, home to many international organisations.

clue.text: Russia begins transforming farming?

indicators.note: transforming means changing form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Russia starts a programme to modernise its agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: agribusiness is farming run as big business.
explanation.definitionFit: Agribusiness is agriculture operated as a large commercial industry, so farming on an industrial scale.

clue.text: Tom sadly has ugly guffaws

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: Great Tom is the famous bell at Christ Church, Oxford, so a tom can be a big bell
the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor Tom is laughed at loudly for his looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom reads as a man's name, but it is a bell, after Great Tom of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly laugh is a deep, hearty laugh, which is what a guffaw is.

clue.text: One values the skilful male version of erotic art

indicators.note: a version is an altered form, so these letters appear in a different order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who appreciates sexy art made with real craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: A meritocrat believes power and reward should go to people of ability and talent.

clue.text: Unable to deliver sonnet, gutted — long to pen one line, on reflection

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the poem

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, as in a mirror
to pen something is to enclose it, as in a sheep pen

parts.note: to long is to desire
Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A poet, devastated, cannot finish a sonnet and longs for just one more line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to deliver' sounds like a poet's block, but it means unable to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sterilised cannot conceive and so cannot deliver a baby.

clue.text: Detest sort of violent crime linked to soldiers

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British assault charge
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Loathing an assault that has been traced back to the army.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a category of assault in English law.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to regard it with disgust, a stronger synonym of detest.

clue.text: Reason Scottish island line brought in charge?

indicators.note: things brought in are taken inside, so these go within another word

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
L for line

explanation.surface: Asking why a Scottish island's ferry route has started charging.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reason or justification for a course of action.

clue.text: Most devious twist I found in exam

indicators.note: something found in a thing lies inside it, so these go within another word

parts.note: a test is an exam
to rick a joint is to twist or sprain it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student finds the nastiest curveball on the exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky can mean crafty or deceitful, so the trickiest person is the most devious.

clue.text: A neurotic drunk — on this?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering what an anxious person has been drinking to get so drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the drink a neurotic might get drunk on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, a plausible tipple for someone getting drunk.

clue.text: Sportsperson's captain never showing pressure

indicators.note: never showing means the letters for this never appear, so they are removed

parts.note: a skipper is a captain
P is the symbol for pressure, removed both times it appears

explanation.surface: A team captain who never cracks under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ps go from the captain, leaving a word for someone on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is a person who takes part in the sport of skiing.

clue.text: Old parrot cradling wing? One seeks assessment

indicators.note: cradling means holding something within, so one part sits inside another

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Poll, or Polly, is the conventional name for a parrot
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: An elderly parrot nursing an injured wing is taken for a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old parrot' reads as one bird, but its two parts split apart to cradle the wing. Poll is the stock parrot name, as in 'Pretty Polly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion poll is a survey that seeks the public's assessment of a party or issue.

clue.text: Former colony, Australian, cheers being claimed by the Netherlands

indicators.note: something claimed by another is taken into its possession, so it goes inside

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands
A for Australian
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: The Dutch laying claim to an old colony, to Australian applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers in British English can mean thanks, as can ta. Natal was colonised by the Dutch Boers before the British.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a British colony in southern Africa, now part of the province KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: See 8
See 7
Modern area in old yard not giving you a turn?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the other word

parts.note: O for old and Y for yard
new means modern
A for area

explanation.surface: A new development crammed into an old yard leaves no space to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: a one-way street does not let you turn and go back.
explanation.definitionFit: In a one-way street traffic runs in a single direction, so you are never allowed to go the other way.

clue.text: Indicates surprised comments about backing tracks

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word wraps the other

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: backing means going back, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: ruts are tracks worn in the ground

explanation.surface: Remarks of amazement about some songs being played in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To gesture is to make a sign with the hands, so to indicate something by motion.

clue.text: Look — big Parisienne runs to the back

indicators.note: sending a letter to the back takes it out of its place and puts it at the end

parts.note: grande is French for big in its feminine form
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tall Parisian woman is told to look and then rushes to the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Gander is British slang for a look, as in 'have a gander'. The feminine is needed because a Parisienne is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a gander is informal British slang for taking a look at something.

clue.text: I criticised keeping oxygen separated

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone admits to harsh criticism that kept the air apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated has been set apart from others, which is what separated means.
